topic: Stock Purchases and Sales: Long and Short
subtopic: Stock Purchases and Sales: Long and Short
source_evidence:
Having a “long” position in a security means that you own the security. Investors maintain “long” security positions in the expectation that the stock will rise in value in the future.

A "short" position is generally the sale of a stock you do not own. Investors who sell short believe the price of the stock will decrease in value. If the price drops, you can buy the stock at the lower price and make a profit. If the price of the stock rises and you buy it back later at the higher price, you will incur a loss.
answer: A long position means you own the stock. Investors who take a long position expect its value to rise. A short position generally means selling stock you do not own, typically stock borrowed for the sale. A short seller later buys stock to close the position: if its price has fallen, buying it back at the lower price can result in a profit; if its price has risen, buying it back at the higher price results in a loss. The source notes that short selling is for experienced investors.
